page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-88-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration featuring high-density local NVMe storage and balanced compute resources. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, providing 88 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 44 physical cores via multithreading. It includes 352 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Architectural extensions include Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512, which provide hardware acceleration for matrix multiplication and vectorized computations. The configuration includes 6,432 GB of local NVMe solid-state storage distributed over 16 bundled disks, without integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing and I/O execution across compute-heavy and storage-intensive profiles. The instance scored 73,268.7 on stress-ng multi-core and 18,439.0 on Geekbench multi-core, situating it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. High throughput is further evident in the Redis SET evaluation at 85.97 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 76.85 GB per second. Cache bandwidth achieved 5,995.54 GB per second on small block reads, while large block uncached memory bandwidth sustained 224.79 GB per second read and 99.15 GB per second write throughput. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,724.0 and gzip compression at 26.3 GB per second, fell within the middle 50 percent range.

This server architecture presents a cost-effective platform for workloads that require significant parallel processing coupled with low-latency ephemeral disk storage. Because storage is bundled directly through 16 NVMe drives, applications avoid the latency and peripheral costs of remote block volumes. The tradeoff lies in single-threaded performance and memory density; workloads requiring disproportionately large memory pools or exceptional per-core clock speed may encounter bottlenecks. The instance is suited for large database clusters, high-throughput caching tiers, software build pipelines, distributed analytics engines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.

Built on x86_64 architecture with support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX, the system delivers strong multi-core processing, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 73,268.7 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 18,439.0. Without hardware GPU acceleration, this configuration is suited for large-scale transactional databases, in-memory caching systems, CI/CD compilation workloads, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks requiring high I/O throughput.
